decisions.text: **#57 stands against F6: a quote the pinned document carries is copied whatever the quoted item's current state; partiality is read from `blyg-partial` in the bake** (session 38, 2026-10-06, Fable 5.1; conformance F6, Alloy 5g(b); studio#29): a pinned thread serves a withdrawn unpinned item's words forever by §8 and §10.4, and the fork copies those bytes, so it adds a place the words can be fetched from, not a disclosure. The "freeze at the withdrawn version" §10.2 refuses is a live, verified quote wrapper claiming a current source; the flattened blockquote claims nothing, and its attribution line points at an id whose live document says withdrawn — the honest state. A SHOULD to drop would need the forker to know the quoted item's state at publish (network, which publish never needs) and would make the fork misrepresent the pinned document. Accepted explicitly; a client MAY note the state when it holds it. Second half: a forking client decides a quote's partiality from the `blyg-partial` class in the pinned `content_html`, never from `>` lines in `content_md` — bakes from clients that predate the partial grammar carry none (studio 0.21.2's call, now the rule). Both sentences are in §16.6f and travel into §5.6 rule 6 at the G11 promotion, which is unblocked. Plan §10.5.

decisions.title: #43's boundary test names its third party — a publisher re-parsing another origin's `content_md`; inherited `[[id]]` links in a fork flatten like quotes
decisions.text: **#43's boundary test names its third party — a publisher re-parsing another origin's `content_md`; inherited `[[id]]` links in a fork flatten like quotes** (session 38, 2026-10-06, Fable 5.1; conformance F7): #43 asked whether a reader or receiver must change; a forker re-parses another blyg's `content_md`, so grammar forms travel between clients and #49 was classed a revision on reader grounds alone. #57 removed the last such re-parse for threads (forks descend from the bake). The remaining case is a forked *fragment*, whose copied `[[id]]` links re-resolve in the forker's context and fail at publish for an origin the forker has not imported — #57 in miniature. Ruled: the test reads "a reader, a receiver, or a publisher re-parsing another origin's `content_md`"; and a forking client SHOULD replace inherited `[[id]]` links with ordinary markdown links to the target's absolute page as the pinned `content_html` rendered it. Publisher behaviour, a revision; the studio's fork does not do it today. §16.6f carries the shape; #43 amended inline. Plan §10.6.

decisions.title: A manifest's address is a path; a query-string manifest is out of scope
decisions.text: **A manifest's address is a path; a query-string manifest is out of scope** (session 38, 2026-10-06, Fable 5.1; Robert Peake's question on blygger-spec#2, queue item 15): a base URL with a query string cannot anchor origin-relative references — resolving `items/x.json` against `/?rest_route=…` drops the query (RFC 3986) — so it has no surface and no stable identity prefix, which is why §12.1 step 1 strips the query. `feed`, `items`, `item` and `pin` MAY carry one, because they are expanded or fetched, never resolved against. One line in §16.6e; a 0.4 construct's text, like the rest of that section. WordPress "Plain" permalinks therefore need the manifest at a real path, which Soapbox's plan already does. Plan §10.7.

decisions.title: A fork's page SHOULD show its lineage; custody runs one hop per fork
decisions.text: **A fork's page SHOULD show its lineage; custody runs one hop per fork** (session 38, 2026-10-06, Opus 5.5; **confirmed by Fable 5.1, session 49, 2026-10-17** — rule 8 is the first explicit statement that verification does not compose across forks, and its wording stands; Venkat stated the intent, "yes" to Fable's recommendation in `pending-calls.md` item 1; conformance F8/F9): Venkat described forks as letting "a reader compare the mod to the source", but §5.6 specified lineage on the wire only; four of five live forks show it on the page, Brady Dale's does not. And since #57 a fork's quotes are unverified, so custody runs back one pin at a time. Both confirmed as intended. §5.6 rules 7 (presentation SHOULD) and 8 (statement of design). Four-question test: no reader change, nothing new on the wire, no locked decision touched (it states #57's consequence), principle cited: #57 and §5.6's own rationale. The reference client already complies (`forkLineage` in `pages.ts`). Ninth revision. Plan `v0.4-plan.md` §10.9.

decisions.title: An official blyg at `blyg.blygger.org` carries everything except the spec and the site's static pages
decisions.text: **An official blyg at `blyg.blygger.org` carries everything except the spec and the site's static pages** (session 40, 2026-10-07, Venkat; Fable review session 40, see end): this decides the "announcements blyg" #15 deferred. **Moves to the blyg:** RFCs (comment periods run there: comments are stubs, quotes are partial transclusions, `stub_of.version` records which draft a comment answered, the version under comment is pinned, counter-proposals are forks); release announcements, **third-party clients' releases included**; technical notes, which are ported; and any other content that fits. **Stays on blygger.org:** the normative spec (#15's three reasons still hold for it) and static pages such as the ecosystem and contributor pages. The reading of #15 that Fable checks: its refusal covers normative text, not non-normative records or invitations to respond. Consequences: a subdomain (not a path on the static Pages site), because receiving mentions needs a live studio and a static export cannot (§15.7); the RFC section of blygger.org is not built; the git file stays the single source for each RFC and note, and a sync publishes new versions, never hand-edited copies; existing `blygger.org/notes/tn-N/` URLs are cited from spec §5.2 and must keep resolving; roadmap-tracks 3.1's generic `/updates.xml` is likely redundant with the blyg's feed, though the per-node "you are behind" notice is not. Open questions are in `docs/fable-round-queue.md` item 18. Nothing built. **Fable review (session 40, 2026-10-07, Fable 5.1):** (a) #15's refusal covers normative text only — all three of its reasons are about the spec; non-normative records and invitations to respond are what a blyg is for; the deferred 1.0 ceremonial pin is untouched. (b) Bylines: the accountable human who commissioned and approved the text is the byline and each item carries one whole-item `generated[]` span naming the model — the TK pattern, since a human approving each item makes the model a tool that was invoked (#38's response-versus-pipe line); the agent byline with `operator` is reserved for items an agent publishes on its own initiative. (c) Porting a technical note changes no status: `blygger.org/notes/tn-N/` stays the canonical citable URL and keeps serving the note's text (not a redirect to an opaque id), because the spec cites it as rationale and #15's third reason applies to what the spec leans on; the blyg item is the same git source published as a thread, where the note takes comments, and the page links to it. **Live the same session:** `https://blyg.blygger.org/` — Worker `blyg-blygger-org`, blygger-studio 0.34.0, Custom Domain mounted at the root, D1/R2 `blyg-blygger-org`(`-media`), secrets `BLYG_BLYGGER_ORG_*` in `.env.keys`, no AI key; on Venkat's **personal** Cloudflare account, not PI's, because the blygger repos stay their own GitHub org though the Protocol Institute sponsors the project; title "Blygger", byline Venkatesh Rao, public responses on so RFC stubs show. Manifest and empty index verified 2026-10-07. Nothing published yet.

decisions.title: RFC-1 rulings: mentions are silent; the shared-origin proof is `rel="me"` between `author.url` and the member's page under the origin; `ids` is a conventional `author` member; the spec says nothing; an RFC becomes its own note
decisions.text: **RFC-1 rulings: mentions are silent; the shared-origin proof is `rel="me"` between `author.url` and the member's page under the origin; `ids` is a conventional `author` member; the spec says nothing; an RFC becomes its own note** (session 40, 2026-10-07, Fable 5.1; Opus 5.5 drafted `docs/notes/tn-6-mentions-and-identifier-schemes.md` (then `docs/rfcs/rfc-1-…`; promoted session 60, #90–#92), reasoning in its section 10): (1) the RFC route runs on `blyg.blygger.org` (#66): thread, version under comment pinned, stubs as comments with `stub_of.version`, partial transclusions as quotes, forks as counter-proposals, a `blygger-spec` issue only for people without a blyg; it becomes a TN of its own by #35's gate (one client emits mention h-cards, a second resolves them) and does not fold into `tn-2`, which absorbs rulings 3 and 5. (2) A mention notifies nobody — #32's principle: a link asserts nothing a receiver could verify; §15.3 refuses or §15.4 fails a plain Webmention aimed at a blyg page; the reference client sends nothing and offers no opt-in (differs from the draft); a client sending W3C Webmentions to non-blyg pages observes three constraints (never into a blyg origin, never for h-cards in baked quotes, never by default). (3) Not an acknowledgement class: #35's reciprocal `rel="me"` unchanged, its origin-side end moved from the origin to the member's page under it; one reader rule with two acceptable far ends, two fetches, two display states. (4) No spec text about preserving microformats; the fix is the studio sanitizer (`<data value>`); revisit only when a second client emits and a sanitizing reader's loss has caused a nameable failure, candidate home §13.1. (5) `ids`: unordered absolute URIs in exactly three wire schemes — `https:`, `acct:`, `did:` (Ethereum as `did:pkh:`, bare CAIP-10 read as the same account) — each `self` or `bound`; a book match is display, never a merge (§13.1 rules 5, 7). **Agent members (section 5.6, Venkat's question):** roster records carry `operator` and `model`; the token scope decides the byline (draft-only → human byline + `generated[]` span; publish scope → agent byline + whole-item span); book provenance is set by the resolver only, never a caller; no pin or withdraw scopes on agent tokens by default. Census re-run 2026-10-07: 20 listed, 19 reachable, field unchanged. Identity semantics, so Fable's under #58. Plan `v0.4-plan.md` §10.10.

decisions.title: RFC-2 rulings: a comments section is the owner's curated display of published responses, every comment a real stub, and the medium's first answer is "from your own blyg"
decisions.text: **RFC-2 rulings: a comments section is the owner's curated display of published responses, every comment a real stub, and the medium's first answer is "from your own blyg"** (session 40, 2026-10-07, Fable 5.1; Opus 5.5 drafted `docs/notes/tn-7-comments-sections.md` (then `docs/rfcs/rfc-2-…`; promoted session 60, #90–#92), reasoning in its section 11; Blygger Studio builds none of it): (1) fits §16.8 and §10.6 on the wire — a display tree from `stub_of` is §10.6's own nesting; the character risk is answered by framing: hosted comments (signed-in, vetted anonymous) are an on-ramp whose accountability the house takes on, and the reference client's responses list stays a citation trail. (2) A bounded cache is fetch-on-display under §15.4 step 5 and §13.5 — the test: if the origin withdraws and the receiver never fetches again, the text must stop showing; durable copies only by pin (§13.4). (3) Unsignalled edits: the house re-sends for its own comments origin (§15.2 permits), kind-1 receivers refresh on a schedule; a spec SHOULD to re-send on every stub edit is rejected. (4) A sibling comments origin is the recommended shape (#61 makes it verify as a stranger would; one renderer for three kinds); it must import the main origin so quotes resolve (§10.2) and run its own endpoint. (5) No counts, no `h-cite` responses markup on post pages (#12, #13, #41, #47). (6) Vetted anonymous bylines `{"name": "anon 7f3k"}` are consistent with §5.5 and #38 on three conditions: mandatory pre-moderation, an irreversible suffix, no `url`/`ids`; the withdrawal link says withdrawal is permanent and visible. (7) Length classifies how much is shown, never whether something is a response (§10.6 rule 2). Gate to become a TN: one client hosts comments in this shape and a second displays them as kind-1 responses. Plan `v0.4-plan.md` §10.11.

decisions.title: A static front page is presentation: a publisher may serve one published item at its mount root, and that item's live HTML pages and pinned pages may name the root as `rel="canonical"`; the item's `page`, document, feed entry and index entry do not change
decisions.text: **A static front page is presentation: a publisher may serve one published item at its mount root, and that item's live HTML pages and pinned pages may name the root as `rel="canonical"`; the item's `page`, document, feed entry and index entry do not change** (session 47, 2026-10-12, Opus 5.5; **confirmed by Fable 5.1, session 49, 2026-10-17**, with the citation corrected — the rule is §8.4 rule 3, not §2.8 — and the reading sharpened: nothing in this protocol reads `rel="canonical"`, readers use `page` and mentions target it, so the link is for indexers and a publisher serving one item at two live addresses names the one to index; now a sentence in 0.4 §8.4 rule 3; Venkat asked for WordPress-style static front pages in Blygger Studio): §8.4 rule 3's "live permalink" is read as the page where the item lives for people, which for a front page is the root; `page` stays `t/{id}/` (#56) and readers, mentions and pins are untouched, so the four-question test is no on 1–3, and the session-20 ruling that §8.4 does not constrain presentation settles it. Reasoning in `docs/v0.4-plan.md` §10.12.

decisions.title: `[[id | label]]` and `![[id | label]]`: an optional author's label after the id, ignored by resolution; any other bracketed text is literal, and a client-private bracket form is rewritten before publish
decisions.text: **`[[id | label]]` and `![[id | label]]`: an optional author's label after the id, ignored by resolution; any other bracketed text is literal, and a client-private bracket form is rewritten before publish** (session 49, 2026-10-17, Fable 5.1; Venkat's session-48 request for author-chosen link text, Ned Twigg's blygger-spec#16 asking for comments inside directive ids, ruled together with tangling, studio#20): the id comes first — the received wiki-link order, #71 — the pipe separates, the label runs to `]]` and may itself contain a pipe, whitespace around the pipe is trimmed, an empty label is none, and there is no escape. On a link the label is the anchor text baked into `content_html`; on a directive it is a comment that reaches nothing — not the bake, not `transclusions[]`, not the feed. Resolution ignores it: the id alone names the target, and a publisher that does not know the form sees literal text. A client MAY tell the author a label has drifted from its target; the protocol checks nothing, because a label is the author's words, not a claim about the target (as `cited` is frozen at the moment of reference). Notification is unchanged: a labelled link is silent, a labelled directive quotes. **Tangling (item 19) gets no construct and no reservation**: its output is ordinary wire, and the rule that a client-private form MUST be rewritten before publish is what tells the two proposals apart. Recommended to the studio, not ruled: do not spell tangling `[[text]]`, because under this grammar a forgotten id would silently mint a fragment whose content is the label. Lands in 0.4 §10.1 because 0.4 is the living text; by #43 it is revision-grade, since readers see only `content_html`. Four-question test: question 2 yes (a `content_md` grammar form), so Fable's. Plan `v0.4-plan.md` §11.2. Studio build is Opus's: the three bracket regexes (`transclusion.ts`, `directives.ts`, `fork-flatten.ts`), the palette, and *copy ID* emitting the long form; a flattened fork link (#63) keeps the baked anchor text, which is now the label.

decisions.title: Received conventions trump cosmetic preference
decisions.text: **Received conventions trump cosmetic preference** (session 49, 2026-10-17, Venkat; recorded by Fable 5.1): where a widely used protocol or convention already answers a question of form, Blygger follows it, and the project departs from received precedent only for a deeper technical reason, never for taste. First application: #70's order — Venkat had asked for `[[title | id]]`; the double-bracket precedent (MediaWiki, Obsidian, whose `![[…]]` embed Blygger already borrowed) is `[[target|label]]`, label-first lives in other bracket families (markdown `[text](url)`, TiddlyWiki, Confluence), and no technical reason favoured the departure. Applies to grammar, wire spellings and defaults alike; cite it when a proposal's only argument is that it reads better.

decisions.title: Version 0.4 opened
decisions.text: **Version 0.4 opened** (session 49, 2026-10-17, Fable 5.1, under #43 with gates G8 and G9 true): `docs/protocol-v0.4.md` is the living text — the 0.3 text carried forward with its section numbers, §16.3 promoted into §5.7 rules 1, 8 and 9 and §15.4 (relation set `stub`, `transclusion`, `fork`, `source`; bound 3 fetches under templates), §16.6e promoted into §4, §5.8, §6.1, §12.1 steps 1 and 4, §12.2, §15.3 step 1 and §15.4 step 2, #70 added to §10.1, #69's sentence to §8.4 rule 3. `protocol-v0.3.md` is frozen at its eleventh revision and flips to SUPERSEDED in `blygger-org/sync_spec.py` in the same change (#23). Plan `v0.4-plan.md` §11.

decisions.title: The pace-layered order is an RFC with reference constants; `pinned_at` is a ruled shape on pinned changelog entries; a pin MAY re-send its mentions
decisions.text: **The pace-layered order is an RFC with reference constants; `pinned_at` is a ruled shape on pinned changelog entries; a pin MAY re-send its mentions** (session 49, 2026-10-17, Fable 5.1; queue items 15 and 16, from Venkat's session-46 ruling that the pace-layered home page is part of the premise): (1) a convention recommended to other clients takes the #66 route — Opus drafts RFC-3 from `blygger-studio/docs/pace-layered-feed.md` with `test/fixtures/feeds/*.json` as its conformance check, Fable edits, it publishes on blyg.blygger.org for comment; the model is what the name promises, the constants (six layers, halving per layer and per hop, one place per version) are reference values a client may tune. (2) `changelog[].pinned_at`, OPTIONAL ISO UTC, only beside `"pinned": true`, self-asserted, absent = unknown and consumers fall back to the version's `at`; a ruled shape in 0.4 §16.9 until the studio emits it (it has stored `pinned_at` since migration 0002) and another client reads it. (3) §15.2: a sender MAY re-send a pinned version's remote mentions; the receiver re-verifies and MAY record pin state from the changelog it fetched anyway; nothing required; the reference order stays own-origin pins only and inbound pins are an extension. Plan `v0.4-plan.md` §12.1.

decisions.title: `cid` on a pinned changelog entry names the pinned document's exact bytes, not a bundle; mirroring pinned bytes is retention
decisions.text: **`cid` on a pinned changelog entry names the pinned document's exact bytes, not a bundle; mirroring pinned bytes is retention** (session 49, 2026-10-17, Fable 5.1; blygger-spec#13, anuraj-rp; queue item 20): OPTIONAL, only beside `"pinned": true`, an IPFS CID of `{origin}items/{id}/v{n}.json` as served; emitting it promises those bytes `author` included — stronger than §8 rule 6, opt-in. Readers MAY fetch from IPFS when the origin does not serve the pin and treat it as the origin's file. A third-party mirror of pinned bytes is within §13.4 and MUST NOT mirror unpinned versions. The bundle was not adopted because its author's own open points (chunking determinism, off-origin media) have no protocol answer; the CID profile and the pin-log contract are a technical note. Ruled shape, 0.4 §16.9, awaiting a build. Plan §12.2.

decisions.title: Author-sized images use Pandoc's attribute form, `width` and `height` only
decisions.text: **Author-sized images use Pandoc's attribute form, `width` and `height` only** (session 49, 2026-10-17, Fable 5.1; studio#37, djinna; queue item 18; under #71): `![alt](url){width=33%}` — the one attribute syntax markdown processors share (Pandoc link attributes, markdown-it-attrs) — restricted to `width` and `height`, bare integer pixels or a percentage; the publisher bakes the attributes onto ``; a client that does not know the form shows literal text, as with an unknown label. The URL-fragment hint was refused as an invented convention; a stylesheet cap is the studio's without a ruling. Ruled shape, 0.4 §16.10, awaiting a build (Opus: parse, bake, size picker). Plan §12.3.

decisions.title: Eight clarifications from the conformance round, and the first member tables
decisions.text: **Eight clarifications from the conformance round, and the first member tables** (session 49, 2026-10-17, Fable 5.1; Aneesh Sathe's findings F2, F3, F5, F14, F17 on blygger-spec#11; queue items 6–8, 10, 11), all revisions by #43, none changing a reader's obligations: **F14** §5 and §6.1 gain REQUIRED/RECOMMENDED/OPTIONAL member tables drawn from the text and measured against one document and manifest from all 22 live blygs (13 item members and 9 manifest members present in every one; nothing live fails the tables; `page` and `author` stay RECOMMENDED/OPTIONAL though universal). **F2** a partial quote's reader re-check is opportunistic and its window closes when the origin stops serving the version; the promised check is the publisher's at publish; quote pins to stay checkable. **F3** the local closure check walks the baked versions, not the targets' current documents. **F5** the watermark survives withdrawal: the endcap is the highest version and a reader keeps it, so a lower or equal version is a replay, not a return. **F17** a line ends at LF or CRLF; a partial quote's blockquote has CommonMark's extent, lazy continuation included; one `transclusions[]` entry per directive, duplicates included; `stub_of.version` is monotonic (keeps its last value, never the creation value); a local id never falls through to an import; `stub_of` MUST NOT name an L0 wrapper id (a `{url}` stub names the entry's link; one live stub does this and is nonconforming — Opus makes the studio refuse it). Plan §12.4.

decisions.title: `ignyr` is a reader-side queue, not a wire member: a same-hash republish is maintenance
decisions.text: **`ignyr` is a reader-side queue, not a wire member: a same-hash republish is maintenance** (session 49, 2026-10-17, Fable 5.1; Venkat's session-34 directive and his session-43 calls that the name stays and agent refreshes carry it by default; queue item 13): a changelog flag saying a version matters less is the significance marker #19 and TN-1 refuse, in the other direction — and the wire already says it: a republish that changed no words has the same `content_hash` as the version before it (§16.6b's re-bake test). §13.2 now says readers MAY queue such versions at low priority and SHOULD NOT resurface them as new; the studio's updates tab names that queue *ignyr*, and an agent's refreshes land there by default because a refresh is same-hash by construction. What this does not give, by design, is a signal to plain RSS readers; that is the one thing the flag would have added and the one thing the bare counter forbids. Venkat was told this reverses the shape he had assumed and asked for it recorded. Plan §12.5. **Extended by #83** (session 50): a version under a reader-local near-sameness threshold is maintenance too, and no token in a note has wire meaning.

decisions.title: Inline fragment authoring: tangling is a studio act whose output is ordinary wire; the author's source MAY be rewritten by an explicit publish-time act; a multi-item publish is one event per item with the thread last and no quiet publish; readers MAY fold a burst; named ids are refused and `page` is the human name
decisions.text: **Inline fragment authoring: tangling is a studio act whose output is ordinary wire; the author's source MAY be rewritten by an explicit publish-time act; a multi-item publish is one event per item with the thread last and no quiet publish; readers MAY fold a burst; named ids are refused and `page` is the human name** (session 49, 2026-10-17, Fable 5.1; the session-29 exploration `plans/inline-fragment-authoring.md`, studio#16 Q3, studio#20 Q1–Q4; salient because Brady Dale's Blynger already chops documents into bursts of 10–12 fragments per minute, measured tonight against bradydale.com, each burst a quarter of its 50-entry feed window): (1) **Option B** of the exploration — rewrite at publish, the wire sees `![[id]]` directives — is what #70 already requires of any client-private bracket form, and the explicit, visible, author-triggered rewrite of the author's own source is acceptable: it is what §5.7 already does to generation instructions. Invisible per-open rewriting stays intolerable (studio#16). (2) **The feed flood is real and is not hidden**: §7 now says one event per item, no quiet publish, thread last; §13.7 says readers MAY fold items an origin published together — same `created` publish, a thread created with them naming them — into one publication with the thread as its entry, deferring fragments to §13.2's low-priority queue, and MUST still import all of them. **Venkat's premise that #77's `ignyr` covers this was half right**: #77 keys on an unchanged `content_hash` across versions and a new fragment has no prior version, so this is a second, derived input to the same reader-side queue, not the same rule; recorded as such. The client cap and visible count the exploration proposed are the studio's. (3) **Names**: `page` slugs are already legal and `page` is already SHOULD-stable (#56); human-readable ids are refused on #2 and §5.1 (collision, identity change across copies nobody controls, squatting, the id in a protocol-fixed path; DOI/ARK/UUID precedent) — filed in `backlog.md` §4 so it is not re-proposed; authoring aliases are a client-private form under #70, ambiguity a publish error by §10.2's logic. (4) **Studio design, not protocol**: pre-flight the whole thread's resolution before minting (atomicity); a blank line after each inserted directive (#49 adjacency); no nesting; a span over §5.3's cap wants to be a thread; no untangle (withdrawal is permanent, §9); the 26-character prose collision gets no escape hatch. Spelling of the tangle operator is the studio's; #70's advice against `[[text]]` stands. Plan `v0.4-plan.md` §13. Third revision of 0.4.

decisions.title: Plain internal links are disclosed: `links[]` on the item document, a fifth mention relation `link`, the markdown link is the one silent citation; reverses #32
decisions.text: **Plain internal links are disclosed: `links[]` on the item document, a fifth mention relation `link`, the markdown link is the one silent citation; reverses #32** (session 50, 2026-10-19, Fable 5.1; Venkat's report of demand for simple responses and his explicit call to reverse #32): a fragment reading `[[id | this]] is right` is the simple response the medium lacked, and #27 is untouched because stubs stay threads. Without a wire member there is nothing to verify, and verifying by scanning HTML for the target URL is the trackback check §15.6 demotes, so each resolved `[[id]]` produces a `{id, origin?}` entry in `links[]` — not a reference (§5.9): a page, not a version, so no `version`, `cited` or `selector`. A remote entry SHOULD send a mention; the receiver derives `link`, last in §15.4's order; a 0.3 receiver fails it, correctly. #32's necessary affordance survives as `[text](absolute page URL)` — same anchor in `content_html`, no entry, no mention, never inspected; the author chooses by spelling. Links are notices, never responses (#80). Forks flatten the bracket form (#63), so a fork carries no entry for inherited links — one-hop custody (#65). Additive, revision-grade in 0.4 by #43; #50's naming condition on the reader affordance stands though its premise is gone. Spec §10.1, §10.3a, §5 member table, §15.2, §15.4, §2; plan §14.1. Fourth revision.

decisions.title: Reposts are classified by the receiver and held with links as notices; verified mentions split into responses and notices; no wire marker
decisions.text: **Reposts are classified by the receiver and held with links as notices; verified mentions split into responses and notices; no wire marker** (session 50, 2026-10-19, Fable 5.1; Venkat asked whether a bare `![[id]]` is a SHOULD NOT — it is not: it is the studio's own repost shape from 0.31.0, and §10.6's misuse paragraph is about volume with nothing to say): a sender's "this matters less" flag is what #19 and #77 refuse, and the wire already says it — a repost's `content_md` is nothing but directives. §15.4, after the relation: strip directive lines, attached partial-selection blockquotes, labels and whitespace; nothing left is a repost. The relation is unchanged (stub-ness comes from the marker, §10.6 rule 2); the class changes. §15.5: **responses** (`stub`, `transclusion`, `fork`, `source`, with words) and **notices** (`link`, reposts) — notices MUST NOT appear in a responses list, MAY show as "linked from" / "reposted by", SHOULD go to a low-priority queue; the studio's is ignyr, the protocol says notice. The test is per document, the relation per target: twenty wordless directives send twenty notices; with a paragraph of its own, one `stub` and nineteen `transclusion` responses. The misuse language stands — the class absorbs content-free stubbing, it does not bless it. Studio: the repost action tells the author the target sees a repost, not a response. Plan §14.2.

decisions.title: The directive label travels: baked as `data-blyg-label`, RECOMMENDED as the attribution anchor, never the target's title
decisions.text: **The directive label travels: baked as `data-blyg-label`, RECOMMENDED as the attribution anchor, never the target's title** (session 50, 2026-10-19, Fable 5.1; Venkat: make `![[id | text]]`'s label the link title "since transcludes also present with links"; premise corrected — the bake has no link inside, §10.2, the "quoted from" line is presentation, so a subscriber never had the label): the publisher's own page could already use it; to reach subscribers and fork flatteners it must be in the bake. One definition now covers both forms — the author's label for the target, shown wherever the reference is presented. Guard against #46: a reader MUST NOT present it as the target's title or as anything but the quoter's words; frozen with the quoted version, checked by nobody, as `cited` is. Additive attribute on a permanent wire token; readers ignore unknown attributes. Spec §10.1, §10.2, §2; plan §14.3.

decisions.title: Quoting and stubbing need no subscription; a client may respond from any URL; the client-agnostic "stub this" affordance is an RFC
decisions.text: **Quoting and stubbing need no subscription; a client may respond from any URL; the client-agnostic "stub this" affordance is an RFC** (session 50, 2026-10-19, Fable 5.1; Venkat: how does a reader stub from a browsing view on any device, browser extensions in mind): §10.2 step 2 said "from any subscribed origin" — a client-local notion (#13, §10.6 rule 7) that had leaked into a wire rule. Now any snapshot the publisher holds from the item's identity origin by §12, by polling or by a one-off fetch; `stub_of.version` stays "what the author saw". Studio: one deep link that takes a URL, resolves it (§12 and the page's JSON alternate), holds a one-off snapshot with no subscription and opens the composer as `stub ↗` does; a plain-web URL opens a `{url}` stub with `cited`; reached by bookmarklet, share sheet (Web Share Target; iOS by Shortcut) and extensions through the same link or the owner API on a scoped token. Real work: `imported_items` is keyed on `subscription_id`, so one-off snapshots need a store of their own with retention rules, since nothing polls them. For a blyg page to offer "stub this" to a stranger it must find their studio — a convention across clients, so Fable → RFC on blyg.blygger.org with a comment period (session-40 rule); received pattern: a registered `web+blyg:` handler with a Mastodon-style remote-interaction fallback. Queue item 23, drafted when Venkat says go. Spec §10.2, §16.11; plan §14.4.

decisions.title: No author-to-machine significance channel in any spelling; the author's lever is the note in words and not publishing; readers derive near-sameness as they derive same-hash
decisions.text: **No author-to-machine significance channel in any spelling; the author's lever is the note in words and not publishing; readers derive near-sameness as they derive same-hash** (session 50, 2026-10-19, Fable 5.1; a parallel Opus session was asked to rig an `ignyr` word into changelog notes for readers to honour and read #77 as forbidding it — correctly): a token in free text that readers route on is the flag #77 refused with a worse spec (`[skip ci]` is the precedent), and "matters less" has its own attack — soften a claim under "ignyr" so subscribers do not re-read, the rewrite §13.3 guards against; Wikipedia's minor-edit flag works only because one origin has admins. TN-1 already makes the note the home of human-readable significance, so writing "ignyr" is allowed as prose; §5.2 now says no token in a note has wire meaning and clients MUST NOT give one meaning (the #70 sentence, for notes). The honest author lever is not publishing: a change not worth an event waits for the next one; held revisions are studio sugar. §13.2: a version whose text differs from its predecessor by less than a reader-local, never-advertised threshold MAY be treated as maintenance — #77 at edit distance zero, generalized; keep it small, one word can negate a sentence, nothing is omitted. Opus: drop the token rigging, build held revisions and the near-sameness rule. Plan §14.5.

decisions.title: A mention's target is known by membership, not location: it MUST resolve, by the receiver's own published data, to one of its items — `page`, item document or a pinned version's address, wherever they live; §15.4 step 2's location test is unchanged
decisions.text: **A mention's target is known by membership, not location: it MUST resolve, by the receiver's own published data, to one of its items — `page`, item document or a pinned version's address, wherever they live; §15.4 step 2's location test is unchanged** (session 52, 2026-10-20, Fable 5.1; Robert Peake's [blygger-spec#17](https://github.com/blygger/blygger-spec/issues/17): on his templated Soapbox blyg every target §15.3 step 1 names lies outside the base URL it required): the "full base URL" wording was carried into step 1 from #61's fix to the *source* check, whose Alloy note said the two checks "should be read the same way" — but they answer different questions. A stranger's document is known only by where it was served, so location is the authority for step 2 and #61 stands; the receiver's own items are its own data, so membership is the authority for step 1 and location was a proxy that §5.8 (absolute `page`) and §6.1 (relocated surface) broke. No host test either — a CMS may put permalinks on another host, and a host test adds nothing membership does not give. Two blygs on one host stay apart by the same test. Pinned-version addresses are valid targets (a third-party sender may name the pin it forked; the mention is recorded against the item), which is the one receiver change: the studio's `targetItemId` gains the pin shapes, and its mount-prefix check is noted as conformant only because its surface is never relocated. Principle, now in the text: a receiver's own items are known by membership; a stranger's document by where it was served. Revision by #43, fifth of 0.4, not snapshotted. Spec §15.3 step 1, §17; plan §15. Opus: the studio pin branch, the Alloy check-7 note, C-15.3-01 at the next clause build.

decisions.title: A sender that does not hold the target's `page` names the target's item document through its `item` template, never the permalink convention
decisions.text: **A sender that does not hold the target's `page` names the target's item document through its `item` template, never the permalink convention** (session 52, 2026-10-20, Fable 5.1; Robert Peake's follow-up on blygger-spec#17, two hours after #84): §15.2's "else the reference convention" guessed `f/{id}/`, `t/{id}/` — paths §4 has called presentation since 0.3 and forbids readers to infer — and the old location test hid it because a default-layout studio happens to serve them; #84 exposed it at Soapbox (does not serve the convention) and at the studio's own 0.48.1 kind check (`remotePermalink` guesses "fragment" when it does not know the kind). The decisive case: a blyg with no HTML pages (§5.8) has no page to guess, so the item document is its only mentionable address. Target = `page` when held, else `{origin}items/{id}.json` via the target's `item` template or the default (§6.1); MUST NOT construct from the convention; the sender already holds the manifest from endpoint discovery. `page` stays first because the receiver resolves both and it is what every live sender sends. Sender-side only, no wire or receiver change; revision by #43, sixth of 0.4. Spec §15.2, §17; plan §15.1. Opus: studio 0.48.2 sends the item document whenever it lacks `page` (item v).

decisions.title: Hopper feeds and the `hoppers` manifest key: a public hopper MAY have a feed and the manifest MAY list public hoppers; not re-emission, because #12's line is the state plane and the `blyg:` namespace, not the manifest; no item document ever names a hopper
decisions.text: **Hopper feeds and the `hoppers` manifest key: a public hopper MAY have a feed and the manifest MAY list public hoppers; not re-emission, because #12's line is the state plane and the `blyg:` namespace, not the manifest; no item document ever names a hopper** (session 56, 2026-11-01, Fable 5.1; Aneesh Sathe's [blygger-spec#18](https://github.com/blygger/blygger-spec/pull/18) for the World Machines bridge, unparking queue item 14): the blogroll is already a manifest key naming a curated list (#13), and §13.5's "no manifest vocabulary" answered whether an imported item becomes a protocol object — it still does not; the feed names memberships, publicity stays the list's. Four answers: (a) no `blyg:` namespace anywhere in the feed, own items included — with `blyg:id` on own items it would be a filtered blyg feed, a refused construct; (b) resolution through the manifest, §12.1 step 7 as a post-condition on steps 2–5, identity (origin, the feed's resolved absolute URL), no channel marker, no reorder, bound unchanged; (c) excerpts never the held snapshot, RSS 2.0 `<source>` for attribution (#71), `pubDate` the time joined; (d) L0 rows scoped to the hopper subscription, an entry that leaves the feed MUST be dropped because the feed is the whole list, following an entry's link through §12 is a separate act. Added: **membership belongs to the list, never to the item** — the sentence that keeps hoppers a taxonomy and not tags on the wire. Step 7 is a reader change, so 0.4 text by #43; a ruled shape in 0.4 §16.12 under #42 (the PR's inline PROPOSED text was moved there), promoted when the studio emits a hopper feed on one node, a second node subscribes to it by URL, an entry leaves on removal, and the whole-blyg subscription is unaffected. Plan `v0.4-plan.md` §16.1. Opus: review studio#84 against §16.12, run the gate, promote under #58. **Built and promoted session 57 (2026-11-01):** studio 0.50.0 (#84); gate run venkateshrao → protocol-institute; §16.12 promoted into §2, §4, §6.1, §12.1 step 7, §12.2, §13.5, §13.6 in the eighth revision, under #58.

decisions.title: The fixed name holds at every identity origin: `{identity}blyg.json` MUST serve the manifest, as the manifest itself or by a redirect whose final URL has the same identity; #51 amended
decisions.text: **The fixed name holds at every identity origin: `{identity}blyg.json` MUST serve the manifest, as the manifest itself or by a redirect whose final URL has the same identity; #51 amended** (session 56, 2026-11-01, Fable 5.1; chrisbodhi's [blygger-spec#21](https://github.com/blygger/blygger-spec/issues/21), accepted as proposed): #51 let a manifest be named elsewhere and then costed reference-following at one cached fetch of the target's manifest, which assumed the fixed name answers at the identity; the three parties who hold only an identity — a receiver verifying under templates (§15.4), a sender building a target (§15.2, #85), a forker checking a pin (§5.6 rule 2) — all probe it, and two clients (Studio 0.48.2 forks, blygd refuses) disagreed about one live origin. The MUST is meetable by the publishers #51 was for: the hosts that intercept `.json` paths serve static files, a CMS plugin can write one, and the directory holding it is the identity origin while templates relocate the rest — which is exactly Soapbox's live shape (`https://www.robertpeake.com/blyg/blyg.json`, everything else under `/wp-json/`). Step 4's direct form stays as discovery. Not taken: a `manifest` URL in every §5.9 reference (bloats every citation for a publisher's omission); "readable only by subscribers" (documents silent breakage). Revision by #43, seventh of 0.4, publisher-side. Spec §4, §6.1, §12.1 step 4, §12.2, §15.4, §17; plan §16.2. Conformance: the fixed-name probe at the identity is a MUST in the publisher suite.

decisions.title: Origin succession: the old origin's permanent redirect of its manifest is the statement of a move; the successor acknowledges it with an OPTIONAL manifest key `moved_from`; readers offer to follow on both, never adopt alone; receivers read a former identity as their own
decisions.text: **Origin succession: the old origin's permanent redirect of its manifest is the statement of a move; the successor acknowledges it with an OPTIONAL manifest key `moved_from`; readers offer to follow on both, never adopt alone; receivers read a former identity as their own** (session 56, 2026-11-01, Fable 5.1; Florian Lohse's [blygger-studio#102](https://github.com/blygger/blygger-studio/issues/102), live case: his 2026-10-25 move and Venkat's stub of a post-move fragment under the old identity, unverifiable at the new Studio): a move is not only a social act. (1) Only the old origin's controller can redirect `{old}blyg.json` — invariant 4's trust basis unchanged — and HTTP already has the word (#71), so no `moved_to` key; a mover SHOULD redirect the manifest permanently and the rest of the surface, and SHOULD keep serving the item documents it published at the old origin, because pinned bytes carry the old `origin` (§8). (2) `moved_from`, an array of former identity origins, after Mastodon's `movedTo`/`alsoKnownAs` and DID Core — the narrower name because "also known as" includes concurrent aliases, which is the mirror §12.2 forbids; alone it proves nothing and gains an impostor nothing, since senders discover endpoints from the identity they hold. (3) Readers: a permanent redirect of a subscription's manifest to a different identity is a move candidate; with the acknowledgement the reader SHOULD offer to follow, without it reports a discrepancy (§12.2's `site` rule); adoption stays user-confirmed; a polling rule, since fresh resolution already follows the redirect. (4) Receivers: an origin in their own `moved_from` names them — membership by their own published data (#84) — with the target matched after substituting their identity for the former one, and §15.4's relation check accepting the former origin; this recovers Florian's case without anyone republishing. (5) Senders change nothing. Not opened: #11, #12. New manifest key, additive, 0.4 by #43; a ruled shape in §16.13, gate: Florian's node declares it, Venkat's mention verifies, one reader is offered the follow. Plan §16.3. Opus: the key in settings, the receiver's substitution, the follow-the-move offer that keeps hopper memberships and signals; blygger.com's two entries for his blyg are the directory's version of the same question.

decisions.title: The studio mods mechanism: three surfaces in cost order — configuration through the owner API on a scoped token, compiled-in extensions in the fixed slots, hooks proposed upstream against a stated bar; no program-hosted extension registry now; the principles are published in the studio repo; a mod is on its own the moment it lives on the first two surfaces
decisions.text: **The studio mods mechanism: three surfaces in cost order — configuration through the owner API on a scoped token, compiled-in extensions in the fixed slots, hooks proposed upstream against a stated bar; no program-hosted extension registry now; the principles are published in the studio repo; a mod is on its own the moment it lives on the first two surfaces** (session 58, 2026-11-03, Fable 5.1; queue item 22, Aneesh Sathe's [studio#59](https://github.com/blygger/blygger-studio/pull/59) as one answer, blykker's five proposed upstream hooks as the evidence; Kyle Mathews against a registry 2026-10-26/27, Venkat for hooks plus principles): (1) **Surfaces.** Configuration through the owner API as an editor would (#31, #52) is blykker's whole phase 1 and costs the studio nothing; compiled-in extensions keep every rule of `docs/extensions.md` (no runtime loading, read-only server routes, writes only through the contract under scopes, nothing reaches the wire); a mod that needs a surface the studio lacks proposes a general slot as a studio PR. (2) **The bar a hook must clear:** *general* — named for what it does, not for the mod (a "book layout" slot is refused, an owner stylesheet for public pages is considered); *wire-silent* — nothing in the bake, `feed.xml`, item documents or the manifest, while presentation of the publisher's own pages is open by §8.4 and #25, the CSS contract's §1 classes living in the bake where no stylesheet can remove them; *reads-only on the server* — a write hook in the Worker is refused, writes happen in the browser through `client` or from outside on a token polling `/api/changes` (#39c). (3) **blykker's hooks against the bar:** public-page presentation and per-thread hiding of feed apparatus are acceptable in their general forms (an owner stylesheet or page-template setting; presentation only); a custom link-section label is a setting, not a hook; **a feed filter dropping marked fragments is refused for `feed.xml`** — §7 since #78 says one event per published item and no quiet publish, the home page's omission is presentation the existing feed-order slot already allows, and the reader-side answer is §13.7's folding; **a server hook on publish is refused** — the general forms exist on both sides already, an extension action writing through the owner session or a tool on a scoped token watching `/api/changes`. (4) **The registry:** not the program's, now, for four reasons — the extension API has no version and no stability promise, so an index pinned to studio ranges is a maintenance promise the program cannot keep (#34's logic: the directory observes, it never vouches); a listing under the `blygger` org reads as endorsement whatever the page says, and the one thing the program's name must not be lent to is code running in the owner's session, which can publish and mint tokens; demand is unmeasured — no third-party extension exists and the one real mod needs no browser code; #47's rule, park on a measured need. blygger.org/ecosystem MAY list extensions as it lists clients, observation under the existing listing rule. Browser-only is a hard rule for **vendored** code because `openapi.json` must stay a function of the repository; a server half is upstreamed or not run; nothing is hosted on blygger.org. What survives of #59, and it is most of it: the operator path — `ext:add` from a repo URL at a pinned commit, the tree hash, the import-boundary and browser-only checks, the review prompt, the build's refuse-if-edited — a registry of one whose index is the operator's own `extensions.local.json`; `registry/index.json`, `registry:check`, `registry:site` and the hosting question are dropped; anyone may publish an index of their own and the program points at none. (5) **Principles** go in the studio repo as `docs/mods.md` (Opus drafts): the three surfaces, the bar, "a mod keeps the studio's generator string", "the no-fork promise is the mod's own, not the program's" — not an RFC (#66 is for conventions across clients; this is one client's) and not a technical note. (6) **On its own:** a mod is independent when it lives on surfaces 1 and 2 and proposes hooks as any contributor does; blykker meets that today; when it runs its own sessions is Venkat's call. No spec text; the four-question test's second question was a yes only for the feed filter, refused by text that exists. Plan `v0.4-plan.md` §17. Opus: draft `docs/mods.md`; re-scope #59 with Aneesh per (4); blykker's hooks (1)–(3) land as studio settings or slots in their general forms. **Batch review, same session:** §16.12's promotion confirmed; studio#106's reading and the tangling plan's two wording fixes confirmed and written as the ninth revision (§10.1, §13.7, §13.2).

decisions.title: An RFC becomes a technical note when its comment period closes; the first build is a revision trigger, not the promotion gate
decisions.text: **An RFC becomes a technical note when its comment period closes; the first build is a revision trigger, not the promotion gate** (session 60, 2026-11-05, Fable 5.1 + Venkat; amends ruling 1(d) of #67 and the closing paragraph of #68): a technical note is a design-reasoning record, not a build record, and both RFC-1 and RFC-2 had their reasoning tested in public and revised in response. tn-1 and tn-3 were written before any build, and tn-3 was revised when facts arrived (#61) — notes already work this way. Holding a closed RFC as neither open nor a note is an orphan state the genre does not have. So the close is the promotion; the note carries a status line (*unbuilt*, then which client built it), and the build gate protects what it was meant to by forcing a revision of the note when the first build lands. tn-2's own gate (#35) is untouched — tn-2 was never an RFC. Numbering follows the note series: RFC-1 → `tn-6`, RFC-2 → `tn-7` (tn-2, tn-4, tn-5 stay reserved). The blyg items keep their ids: each note is v2 of the item the commenters stubbed at v1, pinned, so comments stay attached to what they answered (#66). Plan `v0.4-plan.md` §18.1.

decisions.title: RFC-1 closed and promoted as `tn-6`; a mention's silence re-grounded after #79; `@handle` resolved by the publishing server on every write path; a found-mentions list on the reader's own shelf
decisions.text: **RFC-1 closed and promoted as `tn-6`; a mention's silence re-grounded after #79; `@handle` resolved by the publishing server on every write path; a found-mentions list on the reader's own shelf** (session 60, 2026-11-05, Fable 5.1; comments by Mike Casey and Aneesh Sathe on blyg.blygger.org, anchor blygger-spec#14): (B1) #79 reversed #32, on which ruling 2 of #67 relied; the silence stands on what remains — a mention's wire form is the markdown link, the form #79 kept silent, and its target is a person's page, never an item, so no relation and no `links[]` entry can name it (§16.8, corrected in the tenth revision to "a relation that names a person"). (B2) `@handle` is resolved by the publishing server on every write path — editor, API, tools; submitted markdown may carry it, published `content_md` never does; unresolved `@word`s are returned as warnings to every client; an unmatched `@word` is literal prose, not a rejection. Forced by #63: forkers re-parse `content_md`, so studio grammar must never survive publish. Raised by Mike Casey. (B3) tn-6 §5.6 items 2 (byline by token scope) and 3 (address-book provenance by the resolver) separated, each opening with what it governs; editorial, no rule changed. (B4) **A found-mentions list** (raised by Aneesh Sathe): a reading client MAY list for its owner the mentions found in items it already holds, matched against the owner's own member record (`url`, `ids`), quotes excluded, labelled as a reading-side find apart from verified mentions, no count; nothing is sent, so ruling 2 is untouched. Feeds the owner does not read are refused: telling is the notification ruling 2 refuses, and crawling is a search engine's job. (B5) Opus brief item e is unblocked: the studio's RFC-1 work may begin under B2 and B4. Plan `v0.4-plan.md` §18.2; tn-6 §11.

decisions.title: RFC-2 closed and promoted as `tn-7`; reply notification for signed-in commenters only; no typed stubs on the wire, ever
decisions.text: **RFC-2 closed and promoted as `tn-7`; reply notification for signed-in commenters only; no typed stubs on the wire, ever** (session 60, 2026-11-05, Fable 5.1; comments by Aneesh Sathe, Mike Casey and ksurya, anchor blygger-spec#15): (C1) kind-2 reply notification is accepted as house behaviour, off the wire — opt-in, only when a stub of the comment verifies, byline, origin and link and never the text (§15.4 step 5), the address living with the sign-in record; refused for kind 3, because §7.3 holds no address, an address is the one datum that reverses the anonymity, and deleting it at the moderation decision makes it useless since replies come later; in its place a MAY — the browser token may show a returning browser the replies to its own comments. Raised by Aneesh Sathe. (C2) One install SHOULD run both origins. (C3) The studio's responses list already is kind 1, links only; it is not addable as an extension, since extensions do not reach public pages (#89). (C4) Typed stubs: none on the wire, ever — #10's bag stays refused; sorting verified stubs into display sections is presentation, by any signal a client or genre defines. Raised by Mike Casey. (C5) ksurya's webmentions from non-blyg places are forwarded to RFC-4 (#82). (C6) A #79 notice is never a response. Plan `v0.4-plan.md` §18.3; tn-7 §12.

decisions.title: RFC-5 (enterprise): audience is a property of the origin; compelled removal is a 404 with no marker; group visibility stays L3, with the private-items gate shapes classified; published for comment to 2026-12-03
decisions.text: **RFC-5 (enterprise): audience is a property of the origin; compelled removal is a 404 with no marker; group visibility stays L3, with the private-items gate shapes classified; published for comment to 2026-12-03** (session 60, 2026-11-05, Fable 5.1; RFC-5 drafted by Opus 5.5 session 59, client-neutral at Venkat's direction): (F1) confirmed with spec text (§4, tenth revision): what an origin serves does not depend on who asks — every reader who can reach it gets the same bytes, and reachability is the deployment's; per-reader difference within an origin is L3 (#7), and split-horizon is that by the back door (§12.2). (F2) confirmed, no text: §14's probe clause is already conditional; an allowlisted intended fetch is not a probe; an unreachable source is failed (§15.4). (F3) client policy, no text: §14 already says a quote cannot be recalled; the boundary rule lives in the note; declining a SHOULD for a stated reason is what SHOULD means. (F4) confirmed: enterprise needs no L3 to start; shape E is the trigger, with a named case. Of the private-items proposal's gate shapes, **C2 is refused** (not static; L3 by the back door), **C3 is where the L3 round starts**, and **C1** — a redacted wire, with a fuller rendition off the mount to signed-in readers — is client territory under #3, with one invariant: nothing on the protocol surface names, links to or depends on the fuller rendition, and the public document is complete in itself, the redaction the author's own visible edit (#78). (F5) a sentence in §14, no marker: law may compel a publisher to remove what it promised to serve, or a reader to retain what an origin withdrew; both are outside the protocol; a compelled removal is a 404 with no marker, since a marker is the tombstone #8 refused and invites delete requests; a compelled retention never reaches any surface the spec governs. At close, RFC-5 is promoted as `tn-8` under #90. Reasoning RFC-5 §10, plan `v0.4-plan.md` §18.4.

decisions.title: A private item's first public version is v1
decisions.text: **A private item's first public version is v1** (session 60, 2026-11-05, Fable 5.1; `plans/private-items-proposal.md` §8.2, option (a), confirmed under #19): a publish event is what the wire sees, and the counter is the reader's watermark (#18b); a watermark over versions no reader saw is meaningless. Private history is studio history, as TK's pre-generation state is studio-private under #20; the two counters never meet, and the public changelog begins at v1. Option (b), a public count continuing the private one, leaks a private life by arithmetic. For the build: the studio should not dress private versions in public "vN" chrome. Group visibility (§8.3) not opened; it waits for the L3 round (#93 F4). Also confirmed, no batch review needed: the proposal's §3.3 TK hash-equality rewrite is #20/#44 applied — provenance names the version whose bytes the model read, and byte-equality is the test. Plan `v0.4-plan.md` §18.5.

decisions.title: Changelog display is presentation; a summary reads notes and never text; a note may summarize the history to date
decisions.text: **Changelog display is presentation; a summary reads notes and never text; a note may summarize the history to date** (session 61, 2026-11-07, Opus 5.5; **confirmed by Fable 5.1 the same session**, §18.10, with the clause "or, when the author chooses, the changes so far" added to §5.2; Venkat's request, blygger-studio branch `feat/changelog-display`): (1) Studio settings choose what an item's own public page shows of its changelog — the latest note (the default, unchanged), every note, or an AI summary — and, separately, what the reader shows for blyg items. The changelog is already on the wire (§5.2), so showing more of it is presentation (§8.4 as #25 reads it). (2) An AI summary is written **from the notes only**: notes are public and already obey §5.2's depth rule, so a summary of them cannot reproduce withheld text. It is studio-private — kept per item version, labelled as machine-written with the model named (#59's spirit), never in an item document, the feed or the manifest. (3) An owner may draft a change note that **summarizes the history to date**, this version included, up to 400 characters: it reads the earlier notes and the two texts, under the same depth rule, and is `generated` when published unedited (#40). It is still a note in §5.2's sense — prose describing change, with no wire meaning (#83) — so nothing on the wire changes; the cost is a longer feed entry title. Four-question test: no reader or receiver changes; nothing is added to the wire; #40 and #83 are applied, not reinterpreted; principles cited: §5.2, #40, #59, #83. **For the review:** whether "a note describes a change" stretches to "a note describes the changes so far" — the reading taken here — or wants a sentence in §5.2. Reasoning `v0.4-plan.md` §18.7.

decisions.title: The protocol binds clients, not owners: a client MUST NOT route on a changelog note of its own accord, in either direction; an owner MAY instruct their own client to, on both the reading and the publishing side; the protocol polices only the depth rule
decisions.text: **The protocol binds clients, not owners: a client MUST NOT route on a changelog note of its own accord, in either direction; an owner MAY instruct their own client to, on both the reading and the publishing side; the protocol polices only the depth rule** (session 61, 2026-11-07, Fable 5.1 with Venkat; rules `v0.4-plan.md` §18.8 after Venkat's challenge): #83 protects the wire from acquiring a meaning, which needs a *convention* — clients shipping the rule for everyone, so authors write to it (`[skip ci]`). An owner's standing instruction to their own agent ("if a note says minor, believe it; flag signs of spam") is the owner's reading, delegated, as a mail filter is: the note is addressed to readers so they can decide what to open; nothing reaches the wire, since the author cannot know whether any reader honours the word; and the protocol has no standing over the studio (invariant 3) or the reading order (§13.7). The Smart Feed prompt is already this mechanism. **Four conditions:** no shipped rule, default, template or checkbox routes on note words (the stored instruction is empty; a placeholder may show an example; Opus's "raise only" recommendation is withdrawn as a shipped asymmetric rule); reading only — nothing the client publishes or sends, and no directory, routes on another blyg's note; visible and revocable; the wire gains nothing. **Symmetric on publish** (Venkat): an owner may instruct their client to write words into notes, truthful or not, and the client does not police it — misrepresentation is the author's risk and a consumer problem (§10.6, #36, #80, #28). **What stays policed is the depth rule** (§5.2, #40), because a note quoting an unpinned version breaks §8's promise: the wire contract, not the owner's speech. Text: §5.2 and §14, eleventh revision. Reasoning §18.9; build in `background-plan.md` §3.4.

decisions.title: RFC-3's four items: the model is the convention and the constants reference values; a maintenance version climbs zero; a burst takes one tick; the fixtures move to `blygger-spec/conformance/feeds/` with a CI-checked copy in the studio
decisions.text: **RFC-3's four items: the model is the convention and the constants reference values; a maintenance version climbs zero; a burst takes one tick; the fixtures move to `blygger-spec/conformance/feeds/` with a CI-checked copy in the studio** (session 61, 2026-11-07, Fable 5.1; `rfcs/rfc-3-pace-layered-order.md` §7): R2 because climbing one place is resurfacing in miniature (#77, #83); R3 ruled together with the reader's burst rule as §13.7's one fold seen from two sides (thread first, fragments beneath it, everything else sinks once). The studio builds R2 and R3 with fixtures before the RFC publishes. No spec text. Reasoning §18.11.

decisions.title: `syndication` opens as an OPTIONAL item member `[{url, version}]`, written in place like the pin flag and never worth a version; the protocol specifies no fold and an entry is never grounds to hide another party's post or infer an identity
decisions.text: **`syndication` opens as an OPTIONAL item member `[{url, version}]`, written in place like the pin flag and never worth a version; the protocol specifies no fold and an entry is never grounds to hide another party's post or infer an identity** (session 64, 2026-11-09, Fable 5.2 with Venkat; blygger-spec#30, Patrick Atwater; queue item 27): the claim crosses clients and page chrome cannot carry it (#41), so it opens, revision-grade under #43, named under #71. **Two changes to the proposal.** (1) The proposal spent a same-hash republish per entry on the premise that a member cannot change between publish events; `changelog[].pinned` already does, so the document is rewritten in place and a publisher SHOULD NOT publish a version solely to record an entry (a bookkeeping version sends plain RSS readers an entry with no new writing; #83: a change not worth an event does not get one). The class is the pin flag's — self-asserted, outside the hash and `content_html`, about a published version, nothing acted on — and is not a general side channel. (2) The proposal's fold (entry names the copy, copy links back) is satisfied by a stranger's post that criticises the item and links to it, so a publisher could have readers fold criticism away; the fold leaves the text, as reader-local presentation of non-blyg imports, and two MUST NOTs stay: no hiding or merging another party's post on an entry, no inferring that the author is that account (#11, #35). **Also:** item member, not changelog (the list is copies that exist now); `url` MUST be `https:`, no network-native id (reopen if a second reader shows URL parsing failing); endcaps and pinned files omit it, so forks inherit nothing; an entry carries no counts (§16.8). **Venkat's challenge:** a reader-side rule about showing counts has no ground, since nothing is on the wire (invariant 3, #96); dropped, and the privacy SHOULD NOT offered in its place withdrawn too. **Gate:** one client emits for a real copy without spending a version, a second shows it from an import with no fetch. Spec §16.14, twelfth revision; reasoning `v0.4-plan.md` §19.2. The same session reviewed **tn-4** (gate G3 closed, five edits, no decision; §19.1).

decisions.title: Protocol version 0.5 is Level 3: privacy, encryption and paid access; opened by Venkat's choice, ahead of the trigger and ahead of 1.0
decisions.text: **Protocol version 0.5 is Level 3: privacy, encryption and paid access; opened by Venkat's choice, ahead of the trigger and ahead of 1.0** (session 64, 2026-11-09, Venkat; recorded by Fable 5.2): reverses three recorded positions — the backlog's "nothing before the 1.0 freeze", the roadmap's placing of L3 after 1.0, and #93 F4's rule that the L3 round opens when RFC-5's shape E has a named case. **Amends #6's order:** v0.5 was "Grove" (local RAG and styling); Grove has no wire content, its styling half shipped in sessions 19–20, and its RAG half becomes Track 2 client work with no version of its own. It is a true new version under #43, since encrypted content changes what a reader must do. **Starting design, Venkat's, not yet ruled:** encrypted content goes out on the wire as static files and a reader holding the right key decrypts it; access is fine-grained, per item and perhaps per version; emerging payment rails (x402, MPP, existing crypto) and enterprise sign-on are both ways a reader comes to hold a key; ride-along key distribution (the protocol says how keys are distributed and revoked) and off-protocol distribution are both open. **What stands until the round rules:** #93's classification (C2 refused, C3 the starting shape, C1 client territory), #7 for v1 private items, #11, #12, and "same bytes for everyone" (§4). **Next:** Opus does the fact-finding in [`docs/l3-research-brief.md`](docs/l3-research-brief.md) (tasks R1–R8, findings into `plans/l3/`); the Fable design round follows and rules key distribution first. No spec text. Reasoning `v0.4-plan.md` §19.3.

decisions.title: An item's kind is fixed at its first publication; machine-made items are threads
decisions.text: **An item's kind is fixed at its first publication; machine-made items are threads** (session 66, 2026-11-12, Fable 5.2 + Venkat): a publisher MUST NOT change an item between fragment and thread once published; withdrawal and its reversal are the only change of kind. **Why:** a fragment is a promise to whoever quotes it — one layer, one origin's words, bounded length. If a fragment could become a thread, a quoting thread's next republish would bake in nested third-party content its author never chose and its `transclusions[]` does not name (provenance records direct quotes only, #26); under Level 3 that content could include sealed entries under other locks. Venkat's framing: transclusion is an injection path, a link is not, because a link carries no foreign bytes into a bake. A fragment that must grow is quoted by a new thread, which is the protocol's own way of composing, so nothing is lost. Staying agnostic was the alternative and was refused: a kind that describes only the current version is one nobody can rely on. Thread-to-fragment is refused by the same rule for simplicity, though harmless. **Companion:** a client that creates items on an author's behalf (tangling, any automatic split) SHOULD create threads, because "fragment" is the author's own statement that an item is a leaf and the choice is now permanent; `tangling-plan.md` was revised to mint threads and to drop the two refusals that kept parts legal fragments, and `background-plan.md`'s `burst` rule widened to items of either kind. Readers: SHOULD surface a change of kind and MAY decline the version (§13.3). **Evidence:** the studio API already refused the change (`updateItemOperation`, "kind is fixed once an item has been published") and its editor offers the switch only on drafts; none of the 8 identities held at more than one version in the session-64 crawl cache changes kind (a small sample; the wire cannot show unpinned history). A revision by #43, not a version: no conforming publisher changes, and the reader rule is SHOULD and MAY. Text: 0.4 §5.3, §13.3, §13.7, thirteenth revision. Reasoning: `docs/v0.4-plan.md` §20.

decisions.title: Level 3's first feature is sealed content with locks and grants, taken to RFC-6; payments follow as RFC-7
decisions.text: **Level 3's first feature is sealed content with locks and grants, taken to RFC-6; payments follow as RFC-7** (session 66, 2026-11-12, Fable 5.2 + Venkat; **a design direction, not wire text** — the RFC's items are ruled when Fable edits it and again at its close, #66/#90): the round reviewed research R1–R7 and answered the brief's question D with a layering. **On the wire:** an OPTIONAL `sealed` list of entries on the item document (ciphertext plus the entry key wrapped under one or more locks); `content_md` carries only author-written covers and clear text, with **no new markup**, and `content_html` wraps each cover in a new permanent class (the two-plane pattern of #20); `content_hash` stays the hash of what a keyless reader reads. One mechanism at three granularities: a sealed item, a sealed span inside any item (a phrase or a block; not an item, so redaction costs no feed events), and a sealed item quoted with the existing directive, which a quoter can copy without holding a key. Entries nest (containment, AND) and carry several wraps (any one opens, OR). **Keys:** a lock is an opaque id naming a key; holding it is standing membership; an entry key is per version and is the size of an exception. A grant is a static file wrapping a key to an origin's manifest key or to another lock (lock-to-lock grants carry an organisation's own ordering; no hierarchy or group name is on the wire). A lock's home (a URL, not necessarily the origin) answers requests granted, pending or refused; its ladder — pre-approved, automatic, or a person or their AI delegate — is private. **Identity** is the origin's: one encryption-only key per origin in the manifest, never in `author` (#11 held under those two conditions, to be ruled in the RFC). Sign-on is usable and never required; the Protocol Institute, without it, is the first user. **Payments supervene:** payment is one more ground for a grant, so RFC-6 keeps five things true (per-lock and per-entry request URLs so a 402 fits, a live key-in-response path for recipients without an origin, the home as a URL, per-version entry keys, no price or rail in any document). **Refused in advance:** restrictions on use after delivery (rentals, read counts, metering). Sealed fragments as the block mechanism were considered and dropped for spans. Plan: `docs/v0.5-plan.md`, with seventeen items the RFC must settle (the second hash, key commitment, padding, #52, the second dynamic surface among them). Nothing is built before the comment period closes.

decisions.title: The reader suite's nine open choices, and the clause register's sole statements
decisions.text: **The reader suite's nine open choices, and the clause register's sole statements** (session 67, 2026-11-12, Fable 5.2 + Venkat; queue item 24: Aneesh Sathe's [blygger-spec#22](https://github.com/blygger/blygger-spec/pull/22) and [#23](https://github.com/blygger/blygger-spec/issues/23); measured in session 64 against the studio and 1,767 item documents from 9 origins): all revisions by #43 — readers display baked HTML and change nothing. **(1) A directive line in a fragment is a publish error** — #60 already called a directive with no bake and no `transclusions[]` entry a malformed document, inert-in-fragments would make the grammar depend on `kind`, and since #100 the fragment can never become the thread that would give the line meaning; two live fragments fail at their next republish and no client refuses it today. **(2) The `![[id@vN]]` reservation is of the own-line form**, with or without a label; inline it is inert like the plain sequence. **(3) Code wins, and CommonMark's block structure says where code is**; outside a code block any surrounding whitespace is ignored. **(4) A label is plain text in both forms**, escaped by the publisher (#81's one definition; a rendered label would allow an anchor in an anchor). **(5) A link to an item with no `page` names the item document** through the target's `item` template, never the permalink convention — #85's principle that a guess is never baked into published bytes; §5.8's convention fallback is for a reader's own interface. **(6) An author's relative URL resolves by RFC 3986 against the item's identity origin**, the only base the protocol defines (#14). **(7) A relative URL in a non-conformant source's held HTML is resolved against the source's origin before the bake** — the one change a baker makes to held HTML. **(8) A pin-retained bake carries the retained version**, the highest held; a reader that retained nothing publish-errors. **(9) A baked quote is never inside a `blyg-tk-gen` wrapper**: the wrapper closes before the quote and reopens after (§5.7 rule 3's disjointness), and **the span keeps one `generated[]` entry** — an entry is one generation, nothing maps wrappers to entries, and the alternative gave an agent's whole-item thread quoting ten items eleven identical entries against #66's "one whole-item span"; this reverses session 64's leaning toward split entries, and a checker can no longer test that the counts are equal. Four live items (studio, blyxt) have a quote inside the wrapper. **Sole statements (#23, S1–S16):** MUST or MUST NOT where another rule depends on them (S1 verified mentions off every published surface, S2 sources never in `transclusions`, S3 endcaps omit `stub_of` and `generated`, S4 local ids never fall through, S5 `stub_of.version` never decreases, S16 verification does not consult `selector`); reader MUST NOTs that state locked decisions (S6 no stub relation from the body, #27, with #80's repost test changing class and never relation; S9 the namespace is not a version, #22; S10 a reader does not re-resolve another origin's directives for display); SHOULD or SHOULD NOT for S7, S8, S13, S14; S12's 429 a MUST and "not queued" a SHOULD NOT, being unobservable; **S11 and S15 declined and reworded as description** — a blanket MUST NOT on "diffs or content" would contradict §5.2's allowance between two pinned versions. The closure walk's definition moved into its MUST; §16.6d's heading corrected. Studio changes for Opus: the fragment error, the link fallback, the wrapper split (studio#105), and origin-relative media links on path-mounted nodes. Text: 0.4 fourteenth revision. Reasoning: `docs/v0.4-plan.md` §21.

decisions.title: Unicode on the wire, and what conformance costs
decisions.text: **Unicode on the wire, and what conformance costs** (session 67, 2026-11-12, Fable 5.2 + Venkat; [blygger-spec#6](https://github.com/blygger/blygger-spec/issues/6) and the session-29 exploration `plans/unicode-support-proposal.md`, reviewed with the other three `plans/` documents; measured first against the session-64 crawl cache — 1,836 item documents from 10 origins — and the census's 36 hosts: no `content_md` outside NFC, no control characters, no bidi overrides, every `content_hash` equal to SHA-256 of the UTF-8 bytes, every origin ASCII and lowercase): all revisions by #43. **(1) The hash is over the bytes served, on purpose.** Publishers SHOULD publish `content_md` in NFC; readers MUST NOT normalize an import; nothing published is renormalized and pins are never rewritten. NFC is a SHOULD where the proposal had a MUST, because nothing else in the protocol depends on it (the hash is over bytes either way) and whether a string is NFC depends on the checker's Unicode version. **(2) An origin string has one spelling and origins are compared byte for byte**: ASCII only, lowercase scheme and host, A-label for an internationalized host, no default port, path percent-encoded with uppercase hex, a final `/`, no query or fragment; a URL from the network is put into that form before comparison. MUST, since #61's verification depends on it. Stated as a property, so checking takes no library. **(3) A cap in characters counts code points.** **(4) `content_md` is text**: no C0 controls but tab, LF and CR, no unpaired surrogates (MUST, because one breaks every subscriber's parse of the whole feed); a truncation MUST NOT produce an unpaired surrogate and SHOULD NOT split a grapheme cluster. **(5) A manifest `lang` key is parked**, by #47's rule of a measured need: no live blyg publishes primarily in another language; the trigger is the first that does, or the directory wanting to group by language; RSS `<language>` needs no ruling. Per-item `lang` and a `dir` rule are refused as #46 was. **(6) §14 gains two bullets**: bidirectional controls in attributed strings and baked quotes (readers SHOULD isolate), and look-alike origins (identity is the string). **(7) The conformance-cost criterion is written into §3, non-normative and asymmetric** (Venkat's session-29 no-vendoring ruling read at the protocol level): a rule enters the spec only if a reader or receiver can meet it from a standard library; a publisher is assumed to hold what publishing already takes. The strict form ("any rule, from a stdlib") was not adopted because it is already false for publishers, who need a markdown renderer. It is a test for new rules, not a claim about every older sentence. **The other three explorations needed no ruling:** pour-over links (its wire question was #55; its subscribe-first path is superseded by #82), the rich editor (its byte-rewrite question was answered by #78; a block document model on the wire is refused under #1), publishing patterns (the variorum stays reserved with blygger-spec#8 as trigger; its §10.2 sentence already exists). Two calls left with Venkat in `docs/pending-calls.md`: whether the patterns catalogue is published, and how far the no-vendoring ruling reaches. Text: 0.4 fifteenth revision (§3, §5.1, §5.3, §5.9, §12.2, §14). Reasoning: `docs/v0.4-plan.md` §22.

decisions.title: The payments direction, and five additions to the sealed-content direction
